newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends sharply off on fund selling.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends sharply off on fund selling.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures continued to rack up losses, closing near the day's lows for the fourth consecutive session which saw the most-active March contract fall to its lowest level in three and a half months.

Technically-driven fund selling pushed March to a low of 10.60 and below a previous low of 10.65 made September 12, dealers said. Producer buying on the close buoyed prices off the lows, with March ended at 10.67, off 0.16, having ranged from 10.88 to 10.60.
The other months finished 0.14 lower to 0.02 higher.
Selling accelerated once the March contract fell under sell stops around 10.67.
Today's action mirrored the market's recent pattern of fund selling, which has pressured prices to the day's lows, and trade buying, which provided some light support.
Volume was once again heavy and estimated at 43,488 lots.
"It's been a massacre," a broker said. He added the fund position was so long that when selling emerged, "it broke down the charts so much they decided to go short."
Producer buying was not enough to keep support intact but it managed to slow losses, he said.
The fundamentals are also bearish, as expectations for increased availability and exports, continue to grow.
"We need offtake over the weekend," the broker said.
Earlier, Syria said it bought 13,000 tonnes of raw sugar at $311.50 per tonne for shipment in November.
